summary:
Mersin records no statute, police programme or administrative measure of its own directed at transgender visitors, and no Mersin authority is recorded either extending a safeguard that the national framework withholds or adding a restriction of its own. The province stands under the national framework of Türkiye; the country-level assessment is carried in the national record and is not restated here.

The one region-specific finding in the sources concerns assembly. Human Rights Watch's World Report 2025, covering 2024, records that the bans on LGBT assembly imposed across many Turkish cities also apply to visible LGBT assembly in Mersin-area cities. A trans visitor planning to attend or organise a public event in Mersin should expect the prohibition that applies elsewhere in the country, with no Mersin exception recorded.
tangentialFactors:
Mersin's exposure for a trans visitor is derivative rather than local. The prohibition on public LGBT assembly is set at the national level, and the sources identify no Mersin ordinance, police directive or court ruling that modifies how it applies in the province.

The ban pattern is recorded as uniform across Turkish cities, so the sources show no differential treatment of Mersin relative to other parts of the country. Assembly risk in Mersin is the same as elsewhere, neither higher nor lower.
localsOnly: For trans residents of Mersin, the sources record no municipal or provincial protection, service or complaint mechanism specific to the province. Public LGBT assembly is subject to the same ban pattern as elsewhere in the country, and no Mersin authority is recorded as having challenged or relaxed it.
outOfScopeNotes: Whether Mersin's provincial or municipal authorities have issued their own assembly bans, and on what legal basis, is not sourced. The inventory contains no Mersin detention figures, no Mersin court rulings and no dated anti-trans incident in the province, so what is documented for Mersin is the national assembly-ban pattern alone.
